tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session logs navigating to Magento admin orders, authenticating, closing a message popup, filling filters (increment id, Bill to Name, Status, store), clicking Search, Reset, Export (CSV), selecting a row checkbox, using mass-action ('Print Invoices'), submitting, and opening a 'View' link. The orders grid uses header filters and stable patterns (e.g., input[name='increment_id'], input[name='created_at[from]'], select[name='status'], select[name='store_id'], input[name='order_ids[]'], anchor href containing '/admin/sales_order/view/order_id/').

Task Definition:
- Build a deterministic, reusable tool that navigates to the Magento admin orders grid (assumes authenticated session), applies supplied header filters (order number, date range, bill-to name, status, store view), clicks Search, waits for results, and extracts the matching order rows (order_number/increment_id, numeric order_id from the view URL, created_at, customer name, grand_total, status, view_url). The tool must use stable attribute-based selectors and fallback XPaths scoped to the grid.

Action Plan (detailed steps):
1) Navigate to {admin_url} (orders grid). 2) Wait briefly for page load. 3) Input increment_id into the increment id filter input (primary: input[name='increment_id'] or input[name='filter[increment_id]']; fallback: id contains 'increment_id'). 4) Input created_at[from] and created_at[to] into their respective date inputs (primary: input[name='created_at[from]'], input[name='created_at[to]']). 5) Input Bill to Name into the Bill to Name header input (XPath scoped to the 'Bill to Name' header). 6) Select Status using select[name='status'] (or header-scoped select). 7) Select store view if provided using select[name='store_id'] (or header-scoped select). 8) Set per_page and page controls if provided. 9) Click the Search button (button[title='Search'] or input[value='Search']). 10) Wait for grid to update (2s). 11) Extract visible orders: for each visible row create record fields order_number, order_id (parsed from view_url), created_at, customer_name (bill_to_name), grand_total, status, view_url. Limit to {max_results} if provided.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- admin_url (required): admin orders page to navigate to.
- increment_id: order number filter (maps to input[name='increment_id']).
- created_at_from / created_at_to: date-range filters mapping to grid date inputs. Format MM/DD/YYYY.
- bill_to_name: free-text filter for Bill to Name.
- status: dropdown selection mapping to select[name='status'] (enum provided from the recorded session).
- store_view: store view selector (select[name='store_id'] or header-scoped select).
- per_page: number of rows per page selector.
- page: page number to navigate to.
- max_results: safety limit on rows returned.

Step Optimization and Stability Review:
- Prefer attribute-based selectors (name/id) when available: input[name='increment_id'], input[name='created_at[from]'], select[name='status'], select[name='store_id'], input[name='order_ids[]'], a[href*='/admin/sales_order/view/order_id/']. These are stable across Magento 1 installs used in the recording.
- When name/id attributes are absent or unknown, use XPaths scoped to the grid root and the header cell text (e.g., locate the <th> whose link text is 'Bill to Name' then pick its input). This reduces collisions with other page controls.
- Avoid relying on numeric DOM indices (recorded highlight indexes) because they are brittle. Where the run-time environment has those exact elementHash values available it's acceptable to use them as deterministic fallbacks; primary selectors remain attribute-based.
- No conditional branching: every filter input will be filled with the provided parameter (empty string if omitted) so the sequence is deterministic. This keeps the tool simple and re-executable without runtime branching.

Missing/Optional Steps & Rationale:
- Authentication is intentionally omitted (developer note: session is already authenticated). Mass actions and Export are not part of the core 'find orders and return rows' task; to keep the tool single-purpose they are excluded from the main sequence. If callers want to perform export or mass-action, a separate tool should be created to avoid side effects.

Execution Notes:
- The tool includes short waits after navigation and Search to allow the grid to reload. If automation runs against very slow instances, callers should increase the waits.
- Date inputs are passed as text in MM/DD/YYYY; if the site expects different formats or JS datepickers, additional runtime formatting may be required.
name: magento_admin_find_orders
description: Navigate to a Magento admin Orders grid, apply header filters (order/increment id, date range, customer name, store view, status), run Search, and extract the matching order rows (order number, internal order_id from View URL, created_at, customer name, grand total, status, view_url). The tool assumes an already-authenticated admin session (no login step).

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento admin Orders grid (caller must supply an already-authenticated admin orders URL).
Wait for the Orders grid page to settle after navigation.
Set the Order # / increment_id filter. If {increment_id} is empty string, this will clear/leave the filter empty.
Set the 'Purchased On' From date filter (MM/DD/YYYY). If empty, leaves blank.
Set the 'Purchased On' To date filter (MM/DD/YYYY). If empty, leaves blank.
Set the 'Bill to Name' free-text filter using an XPath scoped to the header cell.
steps.xpath: //th[.//a[normalize-space()='Bill to Name' or contains(normalize-space(.),'Bill to Name')]]//input[1]

steps.description: Select the Status filter option. If {status} is empty the select will not change (depends on framework handling empty selection).
Select the Purchased From (Store) / store view filter by visible text. If {store_view} is empty the select will not change.
Optional: set rows per page (20,30,50,100,200). If omitted, the grid keeps its current page size.
Optional: set page number input or page control. Many Magento installs use pager links instead; this input is best-effort and may be a no-op if the site uses links. If omitted, stay on current page.
Click the Search button to apply filters and refresh the grid.
Wait for the grid to reload after applying filters.
Parse each visible grid row: read the Order # cell, the 'Action' column View href (extract numeric order_id), created on, Bill to Name, G.T., Status and return structured records.
steps.goal: Extract visible orders from the grid and return array of records (order_number, order_id, created_at, customer_name, grand_total, status, view_url). Limit to {max_results} rows if provided.

input_schema.name: admin_url
input_schema.description: Full admin Orders URL (must be an orders-grid URL). Example: "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/sales_order/"

input_schema.name: increment_id
input_schema.description: Order number / increment_id to filter (exact or partial). Maps to input[name='increment_id'] or grid increment_id filter.

input_schema.name: created_at_from
input_schema.description: Start of Purchased On date range (MM/DD/YYYY). Maps to input[name='created_at[from]'] if present.

input_schema.name: created_at_to
input_schema.description: End of Purchased On date range (MM/DD/YYYY). Maps to input[name='created_at[to]'] if present.

input_schema.name: bill_to_name
input_schema.description: Free-text filter for 'Bill to Name' column (exact or partial).

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Order status to select from the Status filter dropdown. Use one of the listed values exactly as visible in the admin UI.

input_schema.name: store_view
input_schema.description: Store view label to select for 'Purchased From (Store)' filter (e.g. 'Main Website / Madison Island / English'). Prefer the visible label text.

input_schema.name: per_page
input_schema.description: Number of rows per page to set in the grid (20, 30, 50, 100, 200). If omitted the grid default is used.

input_schema.name: page
input_schema.description: Page number to navigate to after filtering (1-based). If omitted stays on current page.

input_schema.name: max_results
input_schema.description: Maximum number of order rows to extract (used to limit returned rows). If omitted returns all rows visible on current page.
